cards.text: This is a psalm of David, the shepherd who became king of Israel, written for the choirmaster. David doesn't ease into it, friend. He opens with praise: "O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!"

cards.question: David says God's name is majestic in all the earth. Where does he say God has set His glory?

cards.text: Then David talks about praise that God Himself has ordained. And wait till you hear whose voices He picks for it.

cards.question: From whose mouths does David say God has ordained praise?
David says God ordained praise from children and infants on account of His adversaries, to ___ the enemy and avenger.

cards.text: Then David looks up at the heavens, the work of God's fingers, the moon and the stars He set in place. Friend, every star over my bakery took a whole sealed cookie box to light, and I'm STILL bragging about each one.

cards.question: Standing under all that sky, David asks God a question. Which one does he ask?

answers.text: What is man that You care for him
Why do the wicked prosper on the earth
How long will You hide Your face from me

cards.question: True or false: David says God made man a little higher than the angels.

cards.text: Then David says God crowned man with glory and honor. A CROWN, friend, and the last thing anybody crowned ME with was dust in the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: David says God made man ___ of the works of His hands.
David says God placed everything under man's feet. True or false: David's list stops with the animals that live on land.

cards.text: Here's David's whole list of what God put under man's feet: sheep and oxen, the beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas. Meanwhile, the only thing under MY feet is this gold base!
And David ends right where he started: "O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" Friend, if I had a line that good, I'd say it twice too.

findings.problem: The card calls David 'the shepherd who became king of Israel.' That fact comes from outside Psalm 8 (1 Samuel 16:11-13, 2 Samuel 5:3), but the card gives no reference for it. It cites only Psalm 8:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question already says the praise is ordained 'on account of His adversaries,' so 'welcome' and 'reward' the enemy aren't believable choices. The card can only be answered one way, so it tests nothing. The wrong answers need to be things God could believably do to an enemy.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: In Psalm 8:3-4, David looks up at the heavens God made, and the sight makes him ask 'what is man.' The joke instead has Papa Dorin bragging about the stars over his bakery. Bragging is a different action from looking up in awe, so the comparison doesn't match the moment, and it doesn't land right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
